text:
Maya R.: Heads-up - BlueStone performed a "microswap" yesterday and swapped the owner on acct_4802 for an intro email. It was low-impact but we should decide policy for microswaps so it doesn't scale.

Leo V.: Microswap? never heard that term. what happened exactly?

Maya R.: They changed owner to their AM to send a one-off intro. SF owner flipped immediately, field noticed and rolled it back. No demo/POC at risk but it's a pattern we should guard.

Ivy (BlueStone SI): Sorry, we use "microswap" internally to mean a temporary owner for a single touch. We thought it was harmless. We'll pause any more until you define rules.

Maya R.: Proposal: define two classes - microswap-lite (intro email, <=1 touch) and microswap-full (demo/POC/outreach cadence). Rules:
- microswap-lite: 2h auto-hold, tag pending-microswap, notify partnerships+owner, auto-revert after 2h unless partnerships confirms.
- microswap-full: treat as SI_owner_change -> 24h review + co_sell_role field required.

Leo V.: Agree. Also require the SI to set a reason field on the marketplace call: reason=intro|intro_call|demo_request so we can audit.

Ivy (BlueStone SI): Fine with that. We'll update our tooling to emit reason and set microswap_type. For acct_4802 we will mark it as microswap-lite and let it revert.

Maya R.: crm-bot, can you add a note to acct_4802 and create a confirm task?

crm-bot: Note added to acct_4802: "Microswap-lite detected from BlueStone. 2h hold placed; partnerships review required." Task created: confirm_microswap_acct_4802 assigned to partnerships and owner.

Leo V.: I'll draft a 1-pager with examples and the tiny YAML triggers, share in this thread. Minimal text so SIs can adopt quickly.

Maya R.: Thanks. Keep microswap-lite for strictly single-message intros only. Closing after BlueStone updates their UX and crm rule is live.
